`update_gear` could not change anything about a piece of gear. No tool was added
or removed — the server still declares 109.

This one hid for a while: the gear tools had nothing to run against, because an
account with no gear cannot get any through this server. Given one real pair of
shoes to work on, the tool failed twice over.

## It never had the gear it was editing

To change a piece of gear, the service wants the whole gear back, edited. The
tool was instead sending it a usage report — distance covered, number of
activities, whether a recalculation was running — which contains none of the
fields it needs. Every edit failed.

It now reads the gear from the same address it writes to.

## The edits went to fields that do not exist

Even with that fixed, three of the four things you can change were being written
under the wrong names, so they were quietly dropped:

- The distance limit is stored as `maximumMeters`; the tool sent `maximumMeter`.
- Brand went to a field Garmin controls from a fixed list, not to the one it
  shows you.
- Model had nowhere to go at all.

Garmin stores make and model as a validated pair — you pick them from its own
catalogue — and offers a single free-text label beside them for everything else.
That label is what the app displays and what "Nike" was sitting in. Brand and
model are now written there, joined:

```
update_gear(gearUUID: "…", brandName: "Nike", modelName: "Pegasus 41")
```

leaves the gear reading **Nike Pegasus 41**.

`display name` and the distance limit work as expected now too.

## What else was checked

`link_gear_to_activity`, `remove_gear_from_activity` and `delete_gear` were run
against real gear in the same pass and needed no changes.

That is 24 of the 26 tools that write to your account now exercised end to end.
The two left out are the credential tools, which cannot be tested without an
account password or without deleting the credentials being tested.

## Install

Download `garmin-mcp-ts.mcpb` and open it with Claude Desktop, or drag it onto
Settings → Extensions. Verify the download first:

```
sha256sum -c garmin-mcp-ts.mcpb.sha256
```

**Full changelog**: https://github.com/sedoglia/garmin-mcp-ts/compare/v4.5.2...v4.5.3
